problems.title: Ex. 3.3-3.8 Page faults, instruction restart, and page replacement algorithms
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 3.3 | (5 pts) What does OS have to do when all page frames are being used ... Ex. 3.8 | (10 pts, 2pts for each algorithm) Describe page replacement algorithms including FIFO, First-in Last-out (FILO), NRU, LRU, NFU?
subparts: Ex. 3.3 (5 pts) what the OS does when all frames are full and a page must be brought in
Ex. 3.4 (5 pts) why NFU over LRU
Ex. 3.5 (5 pts) why NFU with aging over NFU or LRU
Ex. 3.6 (5 pts) what the two-handed clock algorithm is useful for
Ex. 3.7 (10 pts) why the instruction must be backed up after page-fault handling, and which instruction
Ex. 3.8 (10 pts, 2 each) describe FIFO, FILO, NRU, LRU, NFU
problems.grouped_with_reason: These six questions are one dependent cluster, not six independent questions. 3.8 supplies the definitions of FIFO/NRU/LRU/NFU that 3.4, 3.5 and 3.6 argue about; 3.3 is the question that page replacement answers and so must name the same victim-selection step that 3.4-3.6 and 3.8 elaborate; 3.7 is the other half of the same page-fault service routine 3.3 describes (what the handler does before it returns). Splitting them would have two workers define LRU, NFU and aging independently and the answers would disagree on, e.g., whether NFU's counter is shifted or merely incremented. They are also adjacent in the assignment, so keeping them together preserves document order. Each sub-answer is still a separate short answer under its own Ex. heading.
